title: Budget or luxury? The same route at both ends
standfirst: The cheapest and the most expensive cruises between Luxor and Aswan pass the same temples in the same four nights. What you pay for at the top end, and what you give up at the bottom, is worth knowing before you choose. This page is part of our guide to [[up]].

sections.heading: What stays the same
paragraphs: The route, the sites and, often, the days. Every cruise between Luxor and Aswan visits Karnak, Luxor Temple, the Valley of the Kings, Edfu, Kom Ombo and Philae, because those are the sites along the river.

sections.heading: What the extra money buys
paragraphs: Space: larger cabins and more room on deck. Fewer guests, so less waiting and quieter moorings. More crew per guest. A private guide instead of a shared one. Better food and better upkeep.

sections.heading: What a lower price gives up
paragraphs: Smaller cabins on lower decks, more guests, shared sightseeing in large groups, and moorings at busy town quays, often several ships side by side. For many travellers that is a fair trade.

sections.heading: Choosing
paragraphs: Decide what matters most to you, then compare cruises on those points. Our evaluation scores each vessel against the same seven criteria, so you can see where a higher price shows.

faqs.q: Is a luxury Nile cruise worth it?
faqs.a: It depends on what you value. If space, quiet and a private guide matter, the difference is clear; if you mainly want to see the sites, a mid-range ship does that well.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest way to cruise the Nile?
faqs.a: A large motor ship, in a standard cabin, with shared sightseeing, outside the busiest weeks.

seoDescription: Budget or luxury Nile cruise: what stays the same on the Luxor to Aswan route, what more money buys and what a lower price gives up.
